Very High Frequency (VHF) Omni-Directional Range (VOR) is a navigation system for planes. It helps pilots find their position and stay on course by receiving radio signals from ground stations. VOR uses frequencies between 108.00 and 117.95 MHz. Developed in the U.S. since 1937 and used by 1946, VOR became the standard navigation system worldwide, used by commercial and general aviation. In 2000, there were about 3,000 VOR stations globally, with 1,033 in the U.S., down to 967 by 2013. A VOR station sends a rotating signal 30 times per second and a reference signal. The phase difference shows the plane's direction from the VOR station, called a "radial." Two VOR radials can pinpoint the plane's location. VOR signals cover up to 200 miles line-of-sight. Each station broadcasts a VHF signal with navigation, station ID (a three-letter Morse code), and voice if available. The navigation signal helps find the plane's direction from the VOR station, and the ID and voice provide additional information.

The national flag of Singapore was adopted in 1959, the year Singapore became self-governing. It was officially confirmed again when Singapore became fully independent from Malaysia on August 9, 1965. Before gaining independence, it was the only state flag in Malaysia without a 1:2 ratio. The flag has two colors: red on top and white below. In the top-left corner, there is a white crescent moon with five small white five-pointed stars. The crescent moon and stars symbolize a young nation rising, universal brotherhood, and national ideals. On the sea, vessels do not use the national flag as an ensign. Instead, merchant ships and pleasure craft use a civil ensign with a red background and a modified crescent and stars emblem. Non-military government ships, like coast guard ships, use a state ensign with a blue background, the national flag in the top-left corner, and an eight-pointed compass rose below. Naval warships use a similar state ensign but with a white background and a red compass rose emblem. There are rules for using and displaying the national flag. People can fly it from their vehicles during holidays and from their homes at any time of the year.

Murray was an Australian electoral division in Victoria. It was in the northern part of the state, next to the Murray River, which separates Victoria from New South Wales. The division included towns like Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, Murray was renamed Nicholls. The change took effect for the 2019 federal election.

Greifswald, officially called the University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald, is a city in northeastern Germany. It is in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, about halfway between Berlin and Hamburg, and 80 km (50 mi) from the Polish border. Greifswald is near the Baltic Sea and has a small river called the Ryck running through it. It is close to Germany's two largest islands, Rügen and Usedom, and near three of Germany's 14 national parks. Since September 2011, Greifswald is the capital of the new district of Vorpommern-Greifswald. Along with Stralsund, it is one of four main cities in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. In 2013, Greifswald had about 55, 659 people, including many students and employees from the University of Greifswald. Greifswald is known for the university, the Biocon Valley around it, the Nord Stream gas pipeline, and the Wendelstein 7-X nuclear fusion project.

Kraftwerk, meaning "power station" in German, is a band from Düsseldorf, formed in 1970 by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider. They are known as pioneers of electronic music and were among the first to make this music popular. The group started in West Germany’s experimental rock scene in the early 1970s. They later used synthesizers, drum machines, and vocoders. On successful albums like "Autobahn" (1974), "Trans-Europe Express" (1977), "The Man-Machine" (1978), and "Computer World" (1981), Kraftwerk created a style combining pop music with electronic sounds, simple arrangements, and repetitive rhythms. They wore matching suits. After Wolfgang Flür left in 1987 and Karl Bartos left in 1990, Florian Schneider left in 2008. Kraftwerk’s music has inspired many artists and genres, including synth-pop, hip hop, post-punk, techno, ambient, and club music. In 2014, they received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, and later won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album with their live album "3-D The Catalogue" in 2018. As of 2020, the band keeps performing.
